Take a quick tour of the gestures
%1$s. It never opens the quick-launch apps; that is the pill\'s own long press.
%1$s (hides or shows the pill by default). It never opens the quick-launch apps.
Portrait: that is the camera spot. It closes the island with the second pill\'s merge, then puts the cards away. A long press there runs %1$s. The glyphs on either side keep switching cards.
A widget that scrolls up and down keeps its own swipes, so use the thin strip on its left or right edge to go back to the apps page.
Long press the camera hole itself, when it sits outside the pill, or the middle band: the normal long press action, so hide or show by default.
Three touch areas: the glyph on the left, the glyph-free middle band over the camera spot, and the glyph or value on the right. Swipes follow your finger. Pull back before letting go to cancel.
Expands that event. On an auto-hidden pill it brings the pill back.

Portrait, with cards on the island: puts every card away at once (the close with its first step skipped). With only an idle widget or nothing on the pill: brings back cards the idle timeout put away, when there are any. Landscape: the pill is not over the camera, so the whole pill expands.
Expands the island (fixed, cannot be changed).
Nothing. Only a long press is handled there, so a stray tap on the hole never expands or closes anything.
Tap or hold the middle band (hole covered)
Same as the middle band above: tap puts the cards away, long press runs %1$s, and the glyphs on either side of the band still work.
The smaller pills beside the main one that show other events. Expanded, the second pill sits on the camera spot.
Brings that event to the main pill and expands the island if it was collapsed.
Tap the second pill, expanded, card has siblings
It shows three lines and opens the list of that app\'s other cards. A second tap closes the list.
Switches to that event, and expands the island if it was collapsed.
Landscape: the pill beside an open card
Tap swaps to the other stored card. It takes the pill swipes and the long press just like the main pill.
Brings back cards that the idle timeout put away. Landscape, while a card is on the island, the circle stays as a small button beside it.
Idle widgets (clock, weather and the rest)
Shown on the pill when no card is.

Grows the pill into the small widget island. Tap again to close it.
Brings back the stored cards, when there are any; otherwise nothing.
Closes it. Taps on the island itself stay on it.
Works even when the pill swipe actions are switched off. The small round circle keeps its own behaviour.
After a long press hides it, or when Auto-hide has tucked it away. Its spot stays touchable.
Auto-hidden: brings the pill back. Idle with cards put away: brings them back. Cards on the island: expands.
Touch anywhere on the open card.
Opens the app the card came from.
Tap the middle of the top edge
Closes things in order: an open picture first, then an open sibling list, then the island collapses back into the pill.

One step deeper. The island follows your finger and finishes the step when you pass the halfway point.

Opens it. With two or more pictures the picker\'s own taps stay with it; the card\'s tap does not open the app there.

Tap the empty middle of the pill, over the camera spot, to put the cards away. Open, the same spot at the top closes the island.

On a hidden pill, one tap brings it back. Tapping the bare camera hole itself does nothing.
The island follows your finger. Change your mind halfway and pull back to cancel.

Swipe down opens long text, pictures and stickers when the card has them, one step at a time. Swipe up goes one step back.
Pull the handle at the card\'s bottom edge to open the app in a floating window.
Buttons on a card are the app\'s own, so Reply, Pause or Stop work just like in the shade.

Take a one-minute tour of the gestures.

On a glyph: opens your quick-launch apps (see Quick-launch window below). In the middle band: %1$s. If the middle band is clear of the camera hole, a long press anywhere on the pill opens the apps. In landscape the pill always opens them.

Where the pill\'s middle band does not reach the real camera hole, the hole sits outside the pill and gets its own touch target (at least finger-sized). If the band covers the hole, the band rules above apply. Notch mode counts as covering: the pill is the notch.
The small circle that stays when there are no cards, mostly seen in landscape. Portrait has no separate circle: the middle band of the pill does its job.
Step by step: text, preview (last text and last picture), reader (all text and thumbnails), then the picture. Stickers have no steps. In these steps the normal swipe actions are off.
Smart Island sits around your camera cutout and shows what is happening: calls, music, timers, charging, downloads and notifications.
